sections.copy_summary: Reason 1, Editor's Pick, and the only entry that is the product itself. Morning static friction turns quick styling into a chaotic delay; dry hair against synthetic bristles generates a charge that lifts cuticles and snaps strands. The comb counters it by releasing a microscopic dry-touch hydration mist as you brush, from an ultrasonic high-frequency atomiser producing ultra-fine particles.

Reason 2, indicting standard plastic bristle brushes. Rigid moulded teeth drag through dry snarls, worsening electrostatic buildup so hair shafts repel one another and fly out into unruly halos. Without moisture delivered at the point of contact, hard bristles keep charging the hair.

Reason 3, indicting heavy silicone hair oils. Thick formulas mask surface roughness with occlusive silicones, creating an artificial shine that turns limp. They weigh hair down under a greasy barrier rather than neutralising the charge, and the film attracts airborne dust.

Reason 4, indicting manual spray bottles. Trigger sprayers eject large heavy droplets that soak some patches and leave others dry. The uneven saturation collapses morning styling, adds blow-drying time, and swells the shaft unevenly.

Reason 5, indicting thermal straightening brushes. Heated ceramic combs expose hair to temperatures over three hundred degrees, stripping moisture from the cortex, burning keratin and causing permanent brittleness. The page states plainly that this device is not a straightener and makes no heat.

Reason 6, indicting fixed bristle beds. Traditional brushes become dust traps of shed hair, sebum and product residue; cleaning them means picking with toothpicks or wire rakes, which punctures the cushion, and brushing clean hair with a dirty brush puts stale oils back on the scalp. The comb's one-click retractable teeth release everything at once.

sections.copy_summary: Reason 7, how to use in three steps: fill the built-in tank with clean water or a water-based essence; press the power switch to start the ultrasonic atomiser and the red light; glide from the tips upward through dry hair to eliminate static and knots.
